payload.title: [crypto-e2ee-2] Replay-window TOCTOU: seen() pre-screen and check() commit straddle await points, so concurrent ...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING crypto-e2ee-2 (medium/race-condition, confidence=medium, verify-votes +1/-0)

FILE: packages/core/src/e2ee.ts
LINES: 861-883

WHAT: decrypt() pre-screens replay with the non-mutating window.seen(counter) at line 866, then awaits #deriveFor() and #aead.open() (real async WebCrypto), and only commits with window.check(counter) at line 882. The commit is deliberately deferred past authentication to avoid forged-frame poisoning. But because seen() does not record and check() runs only after two awaits, two decrypt() invocations for the SAME (epoch,sender,counter) that are in flight concurrently both observe seen()==false (neither has committed yet), both authenticate (a genuine replayed frame authenticates fine), and both return plaintext — the replay is accepted twice. The seam makes no serialization guarantee and MemoryFrameTransformInserter.pump just calls transform.decrypt without serializing, so nothing forces inbound frames through one at a time.

IMPACT: Replay protection can be bypassed for duplicated frames delivered concurrently, defeating the ReplayWindow guarantee the design lists as a core property. Blast radius is limited to duplicate frame delivery (the AEAD still authenticates), but it is a real weakening of the documented anti-replay invariant.

SUGGESTED FIX: Make the per-(epoch,sender) decrypt path mutually exclusive across its await span (e.g. a per-window async mutex / promise chain), or reserve the counter optimistically before the await and roll it back only if auth fails, so two concurrent decrypts of the same counter cannot both succeed.
